body: Angus Taylor had some harsh words for the prime minister this morning, saying Anthony Albanese is “swanning around New York” at the UN general assembly rather than tackling fuel prices at home.

Australians are suffering. And that’s why our fuel price shield will bring down the price of fuel when the price is high … What we see is a prime minister swanning around New York, getting his global citizen of the year award, hanging out with the United Nations, instead of looking at and seeing the pain that Australians are feeling at the bowser and struggling to make ends meet.

Albanese issued robust calls for an end to the Iranian war during his address to the UN general assembly today. Taylor and the Coalition have proposed a cut to the fuel excise tax whenever oil prices are sustained at more than US$100 a barrel.

highlights.title: Estimating suicide risk from text
highlights.summary: A new language-processing tool could help identify the highest-risk individuals from natural language, enabling swifter interventions.
body: When people reach out during a mental health crisis, a top priority for counselors is identifying those with a high risk of suicide. The distressed person’s language holds critical clues, and a new tool developed by scientists at MIT’s McGovern Institute for Brain Research is designed to pick up on and rapidly evaluate those signals.

The language-processing tool was developed by Daniel Low, a former graduate student in Senior Research Scientist Satra Ghosh ’s Senseable Intelligence Group who is now a research scientist at the Child Mind Institute, where he leads its AI, Risk, and Contemplative Science Lab, as well as a visiting scholar at Harvard University. It uses a custom-built list of words and phrases linked to 49 suicide risk factors, searching text for these and using them to estimate an individual’s risk.
points: A new language-processing tool could help identify the highest-risk individuals from natural language, enabling swifter interventions.

highlights.title: Alcaraz felt burnt out after too much exposure on and off the court
highlights.summary: Carlos Alcaraz has admitted feeling burnt out due to being exposed to a lot of commitments before he suffered a lengthy layoff due to an injury sustained in April.
body: The Spaniard, who won the Australian Open title at the start of the year, was forced to miss more than four months from tennis because of a right wrist injury.
Alcaraz returned at the US Open where he reached the quarter-finals before losing a five-set thriller to American Ben Shelton, which finished at 3.33am local time.
Due to the demanding nature of the calendar, the former world No 1 has said he plans to take longer breaks from the game in the future and skip some tournaments.
"With the breaks I cannot plan them in advance," Alcaraz told Sky's Jacquie Beltrao at London's O2. "It depends how I feel mentally and physically.

highlights.title: PlayStation Reportedly Polling Game Developers After Decision to Kill Discs Sparks Backlash
highlights.summary: PlayStation is reportedly sending a lengthy survey to game developers with a question about how they sell physical games after their decision to stop producing physical game discs prompted intense backlash.
body: The death of physical discs will not happen quietly; fans are making their voices heard as loudly as possible, to the point where PlayStation itself is reportedly reaching out to game developers asking for their thoughts on the divisive subject.

Speaking on the Broken Silicon Podcast, content creator, writer, and showrunner Tom claimed that he’d been made aware of a survey making the rounds among game developers from Sony. His sources claimed that it was possibly the longest survey that Sony has ever distributed.

“There is a survey Sony sent out to developers that is, what I was told by my contacts, a bigger survey than they’ve sent almost ever before, if not ever before. And there was a question in it basically trying to ask in a not-direct way, ‘Is there an issue with how we sell games physically?’ or something, like asking developers for feedback on killing discs.

“ Wolverine is still selling plenty of physical copies, and you’ve also got Sony starting to ask devs if they are worried about killing physical [discs], suggesting they realize that if they got a bunch of feedback, maybe they would consider some sort of mea culpa on it. We’ll see.”

highlights.title: Supercell’s monster hunting game Mo.co is going ‘back into beta’
highlights.summary: Supercell’s Mo.co is heading ‘back into beta’ while its dev team rethinks how to proceed with the underperforming monster hunting game. “Mo.co is not performing as well as we hoped…it will need big changes to achieve mass appeal,” said Supercell on its Mo.co blog.
body: This means Mo.co will run “on low maintenance,” says Supercell, and no further weapons or premium tracks will be released. Elite merch and content “will be recycled from previous seasons.”

“Our goal is to release updates more frequently and reduce the wait between them,” the team explained, adding there was no date planned for the next update, but it expected to roll one out before the end of 2026.
“As the saying goes, sometimes you need to take one step back before taking two steps forward,” the team added.

The game’s community manager, Joao, revealed on X that as a result of the change, they will be redeployed to a different role within the company as the game no longer requires a full-time community manager.

highlights.title: Aamir Khan to Receive Screen Icon Award as Singapore Film Festival Opens With Hur Jin-ho’s ‘The Assassin(s)’
highlights.summary: The Singapore International Film Festival (SGIFF) will present its Screen Icon Award to Indian actor, director and producer Aamir Khan at its 37th edition, with a 25th-anniversary Special Presentation screening of “Lagaan: Once Upon a Time in India” alongside director Ashutosh Gowariker.
body: SGIFF executive director Jeremy Chua said the edition brings some of the most respected talents and consequential work being made across Asia to Singapore. “Around it, we have also reconsidered how audiences encounter a festival with new presentation formats and points of entry, a ticketing platform that is markedly more intuitive, an industry programme expanded into a resource centre for artists, technicians and storytellers at every stage of practice, and a new free-to-attend section at the intersection of creativity and technology, attending to the forms storytelling will take next,” Chua said.

SGIFF’s “In Conversation With” dialogue series will also feature Shim Eun-kyung, filmmaker Peter Chan Ho-sun and Hong Kong actor Anthony Wong, who will take part in a post-screening dialogue tied to his first acting role in “My Name Ain’t Suzie.” Korean New Wave director Yim Soon-rye will serve as jury head of the Asian Feature Film Competition, while Fukada Koji, director of “Nagi Notes,” cinematographers Ashizawa Akiko and Tom Harari, and director Jacob Cheung will also take part in the festival.

highlights.title: Microsoft is killing off the ‘Copilot Plus PC’ brand
highlights.summary: Remember when Microsoft wanted everyone to know that "Copilot Plus PCs" were the ones to get, because those were the PCs that that'd have enough built-in AI muscle to get things done? Two and a half years later, Microsoft and Qualcomm seem to be admitting the brand is already dead.
body: Windows Central ’s Zac Bowden reports that even though the new 12-inch Microsoft Surface Pro and 13-inch Surface Laptop technically meet the system requirements for a Copilot Plus PC, Microsoft is not calling them by that name anymore. “These are not called Copilot Plus PCs,” Microsoft Surface CVP Brett Ostrom told the publication.

Kedar Kondap, Qualcomm’s SVP of compute and gaming, seemed to agree that the brand’s time is done, telling Bowden that computers that offer the same experiences will “probably” not use that branding anymore.

It’s not surprising to me that Microsoft and its partners would back away. Back in 2024, smart minds pointed out that ( almost ) every PC would soon contain the basic levels of AI hardware that the brand was supposed to reflect. The flagship feature of Copilot Plus PCs, Microsoft’s Recall feature, wasn’t well received, and Microsoft took flak for constantly annoying Windows users with AI upsells, not to mention the dedicated Copilot keyboard key that you can now finally remap.

highlights.title: Late Gakpo strike denies Klopp winning start with Germany
highlights.summary: Cody Gakpo hit a stoppage-time volley to earn the Netherlands a 1-1 draw against Germany in their Nations League Group A2 opener on Thursday, denying Jurgen Klopp victory in his first match as Germany boss.
body: Former Liverpool manager Klopp took charge in July after their surprise early exit from the World Cup against Paraguay in the last 32 under Julian Nagelsmann.
His side appeared set to give him the perfect start after Felix Nmecha put Germany ahead, but Gakpo finished off a swift counter-attack in the closing stages to level the contest.

The result also gave Xavi Hernandez something to celebrate in his first game in charge of the Netherlands. He was appointed in August after Ronald Koeman stepped down following the Dutch side's elimination at the same stage of the World Cup.

Germany suffered an early blow when Jamal Musiala was ruled out before kick-off, after experiencing muscle pain - and they were given a scare when Virgil van Dijk headed in from a corner inside the first 15 minutes.

highlights.title: Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar gives Google’s AI a face
highlights.summary: Google's new Gemini 3.8 Live update lets users have conversations with the model while watching an animated AI persona respond in real time. The "Live Avatar" will lip-sync and show different facial expressions during conversations, but it's currently only available to Gemini Enterprise customers.
body: As noted by Google, Live Avatar can transition between the 97 languages it supports “without degrading video fidelity or introducing visual drift.” One video shared by Google shows its Live Avatar talking in English and Japanese, with its mouth animation lining up with what it’s saying in both languages. It can also pull up information on-screen while it talks.

The launch of Live Avatar comes about a week after Google revealed its new Gemini 3.8 Live model, which the company says “processes visual inputs in near real-time.” Though Google will offer a library of preset avatars for customers to choose from, it will also allow organizations to create their own. Google says output from its Live Avatar comes with its invisible SynthID watermark alongside safeguards to “respect identity.”

body: With so many games and so many crossovers, it can be hard to keep track. So, here’s a roundup of all the latest collaborations happening on mobile.
Supercell’s Brawl Stars and learning app Duolingo have been building up to a collab for weeks with mascots Spike and Duo trading blows in online comments sections. Now, the partnership is official.

Duo is wreaking havoc in Brawl Stars with a 20v1 boss battle set inside a classroom - where players must take down increasingly powerful versions of Duo and answer quiz questions correctly, or else be eliminated.

highlights.title: I Think I Found an AI Agent Worth the Risk
highlights.summary: Instinct saved me $550, booked my restaurant reservations, and warned me about a phishing scam. It also wasted $64 and might be a security nightmare.
body: One of the first things I did when I left my full-time job at WIRED was give Claude Cowork access to my email and calendar. After reporting on artificial intelligence for years, I was curious about what the technology could do for me. I had imagined Cowork as a hyper-capable digital assistant, but was let down to discover that it was more like interacting with a regular chatbot, albeit one with extra tools. What did I want it to do? I had no idea.

Then Instinct, an invite-only AI agent that communicates with users through iMessage and WhatsApp, started popping off in the Bay Area. It connects to your email, calendar, and messaging apps. Think of it as OpenClaw for normies. The company, which launched in private beta in February, is reportedly in talks to raise $1 billion on top of the $350 million it’s already raised, bringing its valuation to $10 billion, according to The Information.

highlights.title: US edge opening session of Presidents Cup
highlights.summary: The US begin their bid to win an 11th consecutive Presidents Cup by opening up a 3-2 lead over the International team on day one.
body: The United States began their bid to win an 11th consecutive Presidents Cup by opening up a 3-2 lead over the International team at the end of Thursday's fourballs matches at Medinah Country Club in Illinois.
Justin Thomas and rookie Jackson Koivun put the first point on the board for Brandt Snedeker's American team with a resounding 4&3 win over Canada's Corey Conners and Colombia's Nico Echavarria.

World number one Scottie Scheffler, who was partnered with his long-time friend Sam Burns, took the 17th hole and held on to close out their victory over Min Woo Lee and Sungjae Im, who were left to rue several missed putts down the stretch.
And two-time major champions Wyndham Clark and Collin Morikawa ensured the US would take an advantage into Friday's five foursome matches.

highlights.title: The Gigabyte A16 Pro 16" RTX 5070 Ti Gaming Laptop Drops to $1,449 During Walmart's GeForce Week Sale
highlights.summary: Walmart's GeForce Week Sale is ending soon, but there's still time to pick up a great deal on a powerful gaming laptop. For a limited time, Walmart has the Gigabyte A16 Pro 16" RTX 5070 Ti Gaming Laptop for just $1,449.00 with free shipping.
body: The Gigabyte A16 Pro laptop measures 0.77" at its thinnest point and weighs just 5 pounds, which is light for a 16" gaming laptop. It's equipped with a 16" 2560x1600 165Hz IPS display, Intel Core 7 240H CPU, Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 Ti 12GB GPU with 115W TGP, 32GB of RAM, and a 1TB SSD. The Intel Core 7 240H is a 10-core CPU with a max turbo frequency of 5.2GHz. This is a solid, efficient processor for gaming. The RAM is not user upgradeable so it's good that the system already includes 32GB pre-installed. The SSD, on the other hand, is user-upgradeable.

The RTX 5070 Ti mobile GPU performs about 20%-30% better than the RTX 5070. Compared to Nvidia's previous generation RTX 4000 mobile GPUs, it's comparable in performance to the RTX 4080 and pulls ahead of it in games that support DLSS 4.5 and multi-frame generation. The A16 Pro's 5070 Ti GPU is throttled down to 115W TGP instead of the usual 140W max in order to cut down on heat, but it's powerful enough to run most games smoothly on the display's 1600p resolution from classic favs like League of Legends, Roblox, or Fortnite to new releases like Onimusha: Way of the Sword.

highlights.title: It pays to be generous: there’s nothing more embarrassing than being bank-transferred the price of a coffee | Johanna Cosgrove
highlights.summary: If something is under $15 and you buy it for me, I will do the same for you next time. This is called trust and this is called reciprocity. Like many women in their 30s, one of my true joys is meeting a friend for a beverage.
body: The reason that it stuck in my craw is because I firmly believe that you should not request repayment for anything under $15. If we are out together and I shout you a coffee I would rather commit seppuku than be bank-transferred $4.50 ($6 if you are in the CBD, $9 if you are a matcha observant). For context, A$15 is roughly US$10, £8, €9, NZ$19 and 1,680 yen. In this (scary) global economy, that doesn’t stretch much further than a small beverage/snack/Boots meal deal.

The reason my personal threshold is $15 (in the year of our lord 2026 amid a cost-of-living crisis) isn’t due to any market research; it’s based purely on vibes. Twenty dollars? You can absolutely ask for that back. A 20 is a note, it’s (potentially) a meal, it’s a clean, crisp, substantial sum. Anything under? Reconsider your stingy attitude.

Ultimately, at this late stage (of capitalism) we can’t afford to nitpick at the cost of love and care. So please go forth, shout your friends a treat if you can, and remember that it actually always pays to be generous!

highlights.title: Meta employees ordered ‘attorney/client privilege’ hats while fighting child safety disclosures
highlights.summary: Meta's lawyers have argued that certain evidence should be withheld from public view on the grounds of attorney-client privilege in the ongoing lawsuits over alleged harm to teens' safety and mental health.
body: Lawyers suing Meta called the hats an example of its ‘culture of privilege abuse.’

The lawyers suing Meta argue the Project Nido (an internal name for the Teen Accounts team) swag is part of “culture of privilege abuse at Meta” aimed at keeping the research it’s conducted internally on teen harm out of the public eye, an issue that Mark Zuckerberg discussed after internal data on Instagram’s effects leaked in 2021.
US District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers already called some of Meta’s privilege redactions “entirely inappropriate” in an order last month.

She pointed out one example where Meta’s lawyers tried to cast a discussion about a slide deck and whether or not to publish certain data as a discussion of attorney legal advice, deciding that based on testimony from the trial, their reticence about publishing was more of a business decision focused on preventing leaks.

highlights.summary: At least Germany can be sure it will not be dull. Jürgen Klopp had predicted his debut as head coach could be wild, a trait he would accept as long as his team were lively enough.
body: World domination is a far-off prospect for both of these flailing giants on such scrappy, frenetic evidence. But at least those with a stake in this famous old fixture, largely shorn of the spite and spit that defined it of old, could come away feeling something. Restoring those essential sensations of joy, pain and meaning sits at the very top of Klopp’s priorities. Germany looked raw and scattergun for long periods, reined in only by their lack of technical aptitude, but there were signs of an energy that had long been missing.

Nonetheless it was the more understated Xavi, making his own bow in charge of the hosts, who could punch the air in added time after Gakpo volleyed in a wonderful outside-of-the-boot cross from the substitute Ruben van Bommel. It so happens that the 22-year-old Van Bommel is son of the 79-times capped Mark; his grandfather is the former Netherlands manager Bert van Marwijk. An enthusiastic if largely toothless performance from Xavi’s crop was a reminder that the stardust of Van Bommel senior’s day is largely absent now; the equaliser’s conception, though, left lingering promise that the past can birth a brighter future.
points: At least Germany can be sure it will not be dull.
Jürgen Klopp had predicted his debut as head coach could be wild, a trait he would accept as long as his team were lively enough.

highlights.title: Meta is going to let you build games with AI right on your phone

The company today announced two new development tools that will let you create games with AI prompts: Horizon Create, a mobile app, and Horizon Studio, a browser app that offers more granular controls.
body: Horizon has struggled as a platform, but Meta has a plan to give these new Horizon games significantly more reach: It’s going to let published games made with Horizon Create and Horizon Studio get recommended on Facebook and Instagram, where they also will be playable.

“Someone scrolling through Instagram can tap a clip of your game and be in a multiplayer session within seconds, without needing to download an app or being redirected,” Meta says. “Your game lives natively in the feeds where people already discover content and connect with friends.” Games that are “engaging, stable, culturally relevant, and keep players coming back” will get more reach, according to the company.

The company’s announcement comes as Roblox, a similar platform to Horizon that is vastly more popular, is also making a significant push into AI-powered development, including a feature in its mobile app that similarly allows users to generate games with a prompt.

Meta’s news about Horizon, which launched as a VR app, follows a recent pivot to primarily focus on mobile. With Meta stuffing AI into basically everything it can, it’s perhaps no surprise that AI is becoming a big part of Horizon as well.

highlights.title: Arc Raiders Is Testing a PvE Mode Very Soon
highlights.summary: Embark Studios has announced that it will be testing a PvE mode for Arc Raiders next month. From October 13 to October 20, Arc Raiders will have a PvE toggle, allowing you to seamlessly switch between lobbies where you can fight other players and lobbies where players can't do damage to you.
body: Embark will be monitoring the player economy and matchmaking times during this period. The team has noted that "it's possible that this will not work," meaning PvE may not actually make its way into the game permanently. This is a test to see how well they can make it'll operate, rather than some kind of stress test.

"It’s important to mention that this is not a risk-free test," said the studio. "The first, unlaunched iteration of ARC Raiders was conceived as a PvE game, and we have been hesitant to return to that concept. There is a risk that introducing a PvE matchmaking toggle could reduce some of the tension that the game was built around. At the same time, we have to respect that some players want to enjoy the game in their own way, and we can’t ignore what the data is telling us.

"As creators, we design a game with an intention for how we think it should be played; but after launch, it becomes the players’ game. This is one of the unique and wonderful things about making games; we build something with a specific vision, and then we get to see players finding their own ways to enjoy it."

highlights.title: The Horror Show Launches at Academy Museum: Costumes and Props From ‘Halloween,’ ‘Saw,’ ‘Poltergeist’ and More
highlights.summary: Just in time for the scariest season, the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in Los Angeles is unveiling The Horror Show, a major survey of costumes, props, drawings, posters and other artifacts from the most iconic horror films throughout the history of cinema. The exhibit opens Saturday.
body: From Bela Lugosi’s original cape from the 1931 “Dracula” to Aunt Gladys’ pantsuit from “Weapons,” the exhibit showcases classic and lesser-known films from every era. Beloved characters like Freddy Krueger, Michael Myers and Chucky are represented along with more recent titles such as “Sinners,” “Get Out,” “Midsommar” and “The Babadook.”

“Many different types of films can be considered horror filmmaking, from vampires to slashers to thrillers,” said Academy museum director Amy Homma as she introduced the exhibit Thursday. “Horror has its own filmic history, it’s own origins through literature, culture and art and its own lineage.”

“The Horror Show revolves around a simple question: Why do horror films mean so much to so many people?” said the exhibit’s curator Jessica Niebel. “Horror reflects the anxieties of its time, but it also gives us a safe space to confront those anxieties, to look at the things that frighten us and that we desire.”

highlights.title: U.S. Intercedes for Elon Musk’s X Over European Fine
highlights.summary: Federal officials asked to intervene in a case that accused the social media platform of allowing deceptive behavior on its site and resulted in a $140 million penalty.
body: The United States interceded on Thursday to support Elon Musk and his X platform’s challenge to a $140 million fine from European officials, who had accused the social media company of failing to prevent deceptive behavior on its site.

The European Commission fined X in December, saying that by allowing users to pay for a “verified” badge without confirming their identity, X had deceived users. Officials also accused the site of using opaque advertising practices and failing to give researchers access to its data.

The fine was the bloc’s first such action under its landmark Digital Services Act, which regulates how platforms police content. X and Mr. Musk asked the General Court of the Court of Justice of the European Union to annul the decision in February.
On Thursday, the United States asked the court whether it could intervene in support of those legal challenges, according to a Justice Department news release.

highlights.title: It’s sinister that Meta’s Muse AI mascot is so cute
highlights.summary: This is Optimizer, a weekly newsletter sent from Verge senior reviewer Victoria Song that dissects and discusses the latest gizmos and potions that swear they're going to change your life. Opt in for Optimizer here.
body: Meta wants to stuff this guy into everything and entrust it with productivity, health, and relationship goals.

Last night, I asked Blorbo — what I named my Muse AI agent — to help me set some health goals. I was underwhelmed. I’d asked for a workout regimen for a sub-30 minute 5K and regaining lost muscle. It generated an okay-ish but kind of mid weekly routine.

But then I looked at its face. Based on what it learned about me from my emails, it had morphed into cat-shaped piece of bread with a Kirby-like face. It was so stinking cute, it was like getting zapped with the Men in Black’s neuralizer. Until then, I’d been circumspect about sharing too much about my health. But as that cute face gazed into my soul, I started sharing more to see if my recommendations would improve.

I’ve been aggressively avoiding Muse since it launched a few weeks ago. Sure, some of that is because I was busy testing other devices. But the number-one reason why is that I am horribly vulnerable when faced with extreme cuteness.

highlights.title: Over the Hill Is the Perfect Replacement For Forza Horizon
highlights.summary: Over the Hill, an off-road exploration game, is in many ways the anti-Forza Horizon. It's minimalist and chill to the point of mindfulness. It's just you in your chunky little 4x4, roving around a rugged wilderness because it's there.
body: Listen, I love Forza Horizon 6, but it's a lot. It's a lot of content even before you're trying to keep up with the (excellent) weekly Festival Playlist. It's a lot of cars, a lot of notifications, a lot of options, a lot of rewards, a lot of other players. It's noisy. So Over the Hill is perfect counterprogramming — if you can call it counterprogramming when it's also about driving customizable vehicles around gorgeous landscapes.

Over the Hill comes from Funselektor Labs (assisted by Strelka Games), the developer of the impeccably stylish retro rally game Art of Rally. Over the Hill shares Art of Rally 's unlicensed but deliciously toylike renditions of classic cars from the late 20th century, like the Land Rover Defender (Protector), Toyota Land Cruiser (Roamer), and Mercedes G-Wagon (Sentinel). But Over the Hill is no kind of racing game. It's purely about traversal and exploration, about reading the landscape and navigating your way through it.

highlights.summary: After a nearly monthlong delay, states are now able to order this season's COVID-19 vaccines through a federal program that provides free immunizations to low-income children, the US health department says.
body: On Wednesday, Ars Technica reported that the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention had still not opened ordering for 2026–2027 COVID-19 vaccines through the Vaccines for Children program. That was despite the vaccines having been approved by the Food and Drug Administration in late August.

The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) told Ars on Wednesday that “CDC has not yet finalized procurement decisions” for the shots. The department’s statement further suggested Trump officials were questioning whether children should receive them. “HHS and CDC are committed to responsible stewardship of taxpayer resources and to ensuring that vaccines purchased through federally funded programs are appropriate for the populations those programs serve,” the department said.

However, The Washington Post reported late Wednesday that ordering was opening. An unnamed source told the Post that part of the reason the vaccine ordering was held up was a delay in finalizing the CDC’s clinical guidance, which is written for health care professionals and public health officials. The guidance reportedly needed to be reviewed by an external expert.

highlights.title: Google’s Gemini Can Now Make Calls for You on Pixel Phones
highlights.summary: Call for Me—a feature that’s exclusive to the Pixel 11 series—gives robocalls a new meaning.
body: Google has been trying to have its AI assistant make phone calls on your behalf for almost 10 years. Remember Duplex? It enabled the now-defunct Google Assistant to call restaurants and book tables. That service was shuttered a few years ago, but now comes round two, powered by modern large language models.

On Thursday, Google announced Call for Me, an experimental beta feature exclusive to its latest Pixel 11 smartphones in the US (and in English). Pixel 11 owners need a Gemini subscription and have to be enrolled in the Phone by Google app’s public beta. Google has instructions on how to participate here.

These calls are designed to reach businesses. Gemini can call your local hardware store to ask if they stock a specific tool, or chat with a barber to schedule a haircut. Just tell Gemini to make the call—it may ask you follow-up questions for more context—and the chatbot will introduce itself and can have a back-and-forth conversation to ensure your request is handled. If it runs into an automated phone menu, it can navigate it and even wait on hold. On your end, you can view a live transcript on the Pixel and take over at any point.
points: Call for Me—a feature that’s exclusive to the Pixel 11 series—gives robocalls a new meaning.

Rather than following Link’s adventures in the wilds of Hyrule, it would have been a spin-off title in the broader Zelda universe featuring a brand-new, “never-before-seen character.”

highlights.title: Tempeh Is the Plant-Based Food With More Protein Than Eggs
highlights.summary: Tempeh has two things going for it that many other protein-rich, vegetarian foods don’t: a ton of probiotics and all nine essential amino acids.
body: With all that, it’s surprising that so many people have yet to give tempeh a try. Below, a further look at all the reasons to include tempeh in your regular dietary rotation, whether you follow a plant-based diet or not.

Tempeh (pronounced “tem-pay”) is a cousin of tofu. But unlike tofu, which is made from curdled soy milk, tempeh is made from whole soybeans. Because of this, more of the legume’s nutritional properties—fiber, protein, vitamins—are retained.

Unlike tofu, tempeh is fermented, making it probiotic-rich. Thus, it has a deep, pronounced flavor packed with umami, which some people compare to hazelnuts. Traditionally, tempeh is made by fermenting whole black or yellow soybeans with the fungus Rhizopus oligosporus, and then compacting it into small loaves which are then wrapped in banana leaves to age. The technique gives the final product a dense, chewy texture.

Tempeh originated in Indonesia. According to our friends at Bon Appetit, its history “can be traced back 400 years (and possibly more than 1,000 years!) to the island of Java, where it holds great cultural significance.”

videos.summary: Microsoft has filed for a new patent that describes a credit system to "rent" software and games, including rate-limited rentals based on the type of use. In their examples, singleplayer costs more than training mode, but multiplayer costs more credits than both.
points: Microsoft has filed for a new patent that describes a credit system to "rent" software and games, including rate-limited rentals based on the type of use.
In their examples, singleplayer costs more than training mode, but multiplayer costs more credits than both.
Users can 'earn' credits by subjecting themselves to more advertisements during loading screens, round win or loss screens, and level loading screens.
The patent technology can be applied at the application level, OS level, and device level, making it wide-reaching and affecting more than just Windows machines.
